questions.q: What does 'procure to pay' (P2P) describe?
options: The chain from ordering goods to paying the supplier
questions.reason: P2P covers requisition, purchase order, goods receipt, supplier invoice and payment.

questions.q: Which step in the P2P chain creates NO accounting posting?
questions.reason: A purchase order is only a promise to buy. Nothing has changed yet in what the company owns or owes.

questions.q: Which transaction is used to create a purchase order in classic SAP GUI?
questions.reason: ME21N creates purchase orders; ME23N displays them.

questions.q: What is the GR/IR clearing account (191100) in simple words?
options: A waiting room between the goods arriving and the invoice arriving
questions.reason: Goods receipt credits GR/IR; the invoice debits it again. If both match, the balance returns to zero.

questions.q: What is the goods receipt posting on 05.03 for the oak?
questions.reason: The oak (80,000) enters inventory, and the value waits in GR/IR until the invoice arrives.

questions.q: Where does the DKK 80,000 value of the goods receipt come from?
options: The purchase order: 20 m³ at DKK 4,000
questions.reason: At goods receipt there is no invoice yet, so the value is taken from the PO price and the received quantity.

questions.q: What is posted when Maria enters the oak invoice in MIRO?
options: Debit GR/IR 80,000 and Input VAT 20,000; Credit Payables (Jysk Træ) 100,000
Nothing; MIRO only checks the invoice
questions.reason: The invoice empties GR/IR, records the VAT to reclaim, and creates a DKK 100,000 debt to the supplier.

questions.q: What does the three-way match compare?
options: Purchase order, goods receipt and invoice
Invoice, bank statement and VAT return
Cost centre, profit centre and GL account
questions.reason: MIRO checks what was ordered, what was received and what is being charged, for quantity and price.

questions.q: Jysk Træ invoices DKK 4,200 per m³ instead of 4,000, far above tolerance. What usually happens?
options: The invoice is posted but blocked for payment until someone releases it
The supplier is paid the higher price at once
questions.reason: A difference above tolerance sets a payment block (R). The invoice can be released in MRBR after checking.

questions.q: Which transaction releases invoices blocked for price or quantity differences?
questions.reason: MRBR releases blocked invoices from logistics invoice verification.

questions.q: Which transaction is used for a supplier invoice WITHOUT a purchase order, such as a cleaning bill?
questions.reason: FB60 enters supplier invoices directly in FI; the clerk chooses the expense account.

questions.q: Why do FB60 invoices often need an approval step?
options: There is no PO or goods receipt, so no three-way match protects them
Because they are always foreign currency
Because the payment run cannot pay them
questions.reason: Without a PO there is nothing to match against, so someone must confirm the service was delivered.

questions.q: What is a reconciliation account such as 160000?
options: A GL account that shows the total of all supplier sub-ledgers
A separate bank account for each supplier
An account you post to manually every day
questions.reason: Each supplier has its own sub-ledger; 160000 collects the total automatically and is not posted to directly.

questions.q: In S/4HANA, how is a supplier like Jysk Træ maintained?
options: As a Business Partner with the supplier role, in transaction BP
Only as a GL account in FS00
questions.reason: Suppliers and customers are Business Partners; the supplier role and company code data hold AP settings.

questions.q: In Denmark, how is a company's VAT number usually formed?
options: The postcode followed by the city
questions.reason: The CVR number is the Danish company registration number; the VAT number is DK plus the CVR number.

questions.q: The invoice is dated 08.03 with 30 days net. When is it due?
questions.reason: 8 March plus 30 days is 7 April.

questions.q: Why is the oak invoice paid in the run on 06.04, one day before the due date?
options: It is due before the next run date (13.04), so waiting would make it late
Because all invoices are paid immediately
Because the payment run only runs once a year
questions.reason: F110 pays items due before the next run date. Waiting until 13.04 would pay six days late.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the F110 steps?
options: Parameters, proposal, review, payment run, payment medium
questions.reason: First set parameters, then build and check a proposal, then post the payments and create the bank file.

questions.q: What is the payment posting on 06.04?
questions.reason: Paying reduces the debt to the supplier (debit) and the bank balance (credit), and clears the open item.

questions.q: What is ISO 20022 pain.001?
options: A standard XML file format for sending payment orders to the bank
questions.reason: F110's payment medium step writes a pain.001 file that the bank reads to make the transfers.

questions.q: After goods receipt, invoice and payment, what is the GR/IR balance for the oak?
questions.reason: GR/IR was credited 80,000 at goods receipt and debited 80,000 at the invoice, so it is back to zero.

questions.q: After the full cycle, what is the balance on 154000 Input VAT, and what happens to it?
options: DKK 20,000 debit, reclaimed in the VAT return
DKK 0, it was paid to the supplier and forgotten
DKK 100,000 credit, owed to the bank
questions.reason: Nordlys paid 20,000 VAT to Jysk Træ and can claim it back from the tax agency as input VAT.

questions.q: What does the duplicate invoice check look at?
options: Fields such as supplier, invoice reference, date and amount already entered
questions.reason: If the same supplier, reference, date and amount were already entered, SAP warns or stops the second entry.

questions.q: An email 'from Jysk Træ' asks to change its bank account. What is the safe response?
options: Verify by calling the supplier on a known number, and use dual control for the change
Change it right away to avoid late payment
Pay into both accounts to be sure
questions.reason: Bank detail changes are a classic fraud route; many projects require a second person to confirm sensitive changes.

questions.q: Terms are '2% within 8 days, 30 days net' on a DKK 100,000 invoice dated 08.03. What does paying by 16.03 cost?
questions.reason: Paying within 8 days allows a 2% cash discount: 100,000 minus 2,000 is 98,000.

questions.q: What is an FI-kort payment line (+71, +73, +75) in Denmark?
options: A Danish payment slip format with a creditor number and often a payment reference
questions.reason: Many Danish bills carry an FI-kort line; for +71 and +75 the reference tells the supplier which invoice is paid.
